title: I Printed the Trivia-Night Buzzer Policy After They Wired a Second

parts.text: I sat trivia at 7:32 p.m. and the table next to us dinged twice as fast. The buzzer policy the host laminated said: ONE SYSTEM PER TEAM. HOUSE GEAR ONLY. I was twenty-nine, team captain, holding a house clicker that felt honest. The other captain said, "Backup for lag." I could see a second dongle. I photographed the dongle, the laminate, and our clicker. Then I printed the policy at the bar printer and handed it to the host with the photo. At 7:38 the host asked why that table was on a dual-buzzer ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The host can see a second dongle against the one-system laminate he posted.

social.video_title: They wired a second trivia buzzer for lag — Part 1/2
social.description: House clicker, a double ding, and a laminate. I printed the policy at the bar. Would you have played through?

parts.text: They called it a stream deck until the host pulled the extra dongle. I kept the ticket, the laminate, and the photo. We played even. They told the league the policy was always about optics. Optics is a word captains use when a dongle exists. Buzzer policy now has a second line: LAG IS NOT A SECOND SYSTEM. I click once. They use house gear. The ding finally means one team.

social.video_title: Lag is not a second buzzer — Part 2/2
social.description: Dual-buzzer ticket, a pulled dongle, and a second line on the laminate. Was backup ever a cheat?
